title: "Figures"

Figure scripts read the aggregated results under `<DATA_ROOT>/data/outputs/` and write
to `50_plots/`. None of them fit a model, so they run in seconds to minutes.

| Script | Produces | Reads |
|--------|----------|-------|

## Figure 4: which values are averaged

`54_fig-4+supptable_vpd_response_curve_shap_agg.py` sets `aggfunc = 'mean'`. That is what the SHAP
values are aggregated with, matching the manuscript.

The script also sets `median` for two columns, which is easy to misread as median
aggregation of the results:

```python
# Bins always use 'median', b/c using 'mean' results in floating point errors
xagg = 'median' if str(xvar).startswith('BIN_') else aggfunc
yagg = 'median' if str(xvar).startswith('BIN_') else aggfunc
xcol, ycol, zcol = (f"{xvar}", xagg), (f"{yvar}", yagg), (f"{zvar}", aggfunc)
```

`xagg` and `yagg` apply to the bin coordinate columns only. Every record in a bin
carries the same bin edge, so mean and median return the same number, and the median is
used because averaging identical floats reintroduces rounding noise in the labels. The
SHAP values themselves, `zcol`, use `aggfunc`.

## Table 1 and its figure: seventeen tests, nine of them in the main text

`55_table-1+suppfig_threshold_robustness.py` computes nothing. Script 47 builds the rows and
writes them to `47_THRESHOLD_Robustness_NEP_ZSCORE.csv`, and script 55 reads that file and
renders it twice, as the main-text table and as the supplementary figure, so the two cannot
disagree.

Seventeen tests in three groups, with the published analysis on top as the reference row:

| Group | Tests |
|---|---|
| Soil water depth | deepest available layer at all sites; the 128 matched sites on layer 1; the same sites on their deepest layer; the 59 sites that reached layer 5 or deeper, on layer 1 and on their deep layer |
| Model fitting | air temperature dropped from the predictor set; blocked cross-validation; ALE instead of SHAP; the threshold estimator across 23 settings |
| Site set | any one site removed; Europe removed; North America removed; both removed; records of at least 3, 5 and 10 years |

Each row carries the test, the number of sites, the threshold in sigma and in kPa, and an
interval. Both units, because every row converts sigma to kPa using its own site set: a row
can move in kPa while standing still in sigma, and kPa alone hides that. Sigma is also what
Figure 4 and the coefficient table report. The interval is the 95 % prediction band of the fitted polynomial, the same one
Figure 4 and the coefficient table show, so the reference row reads 1.26 [1.16, 1.36] in all
three places. Script 47 also writes a bootstrap over sites, about five times narrower, in
`boot_lower` and `boot_upper`. That one is not shown here, because two intervals on the same
number would confuse a reader.

Three rows have no band, and the figure and the table both say so rather than leaving it to
the caption. The estimator row carries the spread across its 23 settings, and the
leave-one-site-out row the spread across its 208 removals, which share 207 sites with each
other and are not independent draws. The ALE row has no curve fitted here at all, since stage
46 derives its value as a mean of per-site crossings. In the figure those rows are drawn with
whiskers instead of a bar. In the value column they read `1.26 (1.23 to 1.30 range)` and
`1.25 (no band)`, so square brackets mean a prediction band and round brackets mean anything
else. The table marks them with an asterisk as well.

**The main table takes nine of the seventeen**, one per kind of challenge: the layer 5+ pair,
air temperature dropped, blocked cross-validation, the GAM, ALE, any one site removed, North
America removed, and records of at least 10 years. Depth is the one theme that takes two rows,
because the pair is the comparison. `MAIN_ROWS` in script 55 holds that list. The rest
are redundant in a main display item, since three record-length rows make one point, three
region rows make one point, and each matched pair argues one comparison over two rows. Both
largest movers stay in, so the selection cannot be read as flattering, and the estimator row
goes out, which leaves the interval column with two meanings instead of three. The
supplementary figure keeps all seventeen, and the table footnote points at it.

**The deepest-layer pair.** The matched rows use all 128 sites that moved down, and most moved
one layer, so the depth contrast is small. The pair restricted to the 59 sites that reached
layer 5 or deeper holds the sites fixed and gives the largest contrast the network allows:
1.195 kPa on layer 1 against 1.207 on their deep layer, so depth moves the threshold by
0.012 kPa. Both sit about 0.06 kPa below the published value, which is those 59 sites being a
different sample rather than a depth effect. That is why the row is a pair.

**Neither shows a shift column.** Rounded to two decimals several of the shifts read as +0.00
or -0.00, and three decimals would claim a precision the interval does not support. An earlier
version of the figure plotted the shift on an axis centred on the published value, which made
agreement easy to see but hid the numbers a reader wants to quote. It now uses an absolute kPa
axis with the value printed beside each row.

**The figure is a table and a plot side by side**, the same rows in both halves: label, sites,
threshold and interval on the left, bars on the right, one shared row grid. A rule sits under
the reference row so the value being tested is separate from the tests. Everything is one
blue. Colouring the two largest movers red made seventeen agreeing rows look like a list of
passes and failures, which is the opposite of what the figure says.

Output is one png, one xlsx for pasting into Word, and one csv of the same table.

## Script 57: configuration

The ALE response curve script has the most switches. Options at the top of the file:

| Setting | Default | Effect |
|---------|---------|--------|
| `PLOT_FEATURE` | `VPD_ZSCORE` | Feature on the x axis |
| `FLUX` | `NEP_ZSCORE` | Target |
| `USE_MEDIAN` | `False` | Mean aggregation across sites; `True` switches to median |
| `USE_CI` | `True` | Labels show a 95 % interval; `False` shows the standard error |
| `VARIANT` | `""` | Reads the matching run variant and writes beside it |

Output is one figure: a large panel with every site curve in grey and a marker at the mean
zero crossing, and four panels splitting the same data by IGBP type (ENF, DBF, MF, EBF).
It writes nothing else. The curves and the threshold table come from script 46, which has
to run first.
